newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SICOM's tax holiday extended for five more years.
newsitem.headline: SICOM's tax holiday extended for five more years.

text.p: The Singapore Commodity Exchange's (SICOM) five year tax holiday will be extended for five years, Finance Minister Richard Hu said on Friday.
"As the exchange is still in the development stage, I have decided to extend the tax holiday granted to SICOM for another five years," Hu said.
SICOM was granted a five year tax holiday when it was established in 1992 to allow the exchange to get off to a successful start, the minster said.
Hu also said in addition to existing income items which qualify for a tax holiday, new items which have arisen from the exchange's development will be exempt.

This includes fees for quality assurance of physical commodities, registration fees for nominated warehouses, fees for the processing of applications and annual subscription fees for registered representatives and associated persons, local membership processing fees, fees for leases of seats on SICOM and proceeds from the sales of trading permit.
